extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers; journalists and news editors (WWII-era)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and constraints relevant to wartime news reporting and government communications (e.g., censorship restrictions and internal press-office conduct). Useful for journalists, wire services, and government public-information staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: O.W.I. press engagement guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: "From now on, I hope, O. W. I. can keep out of the newspapers except for our end product—the encouragement and enlightenment of our friends abroad and the discouragement of the enemy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction from the Office of War Information director to overseas branch employees to avoid publicity about the agency itself and limit press presence to finished public-facing material; implies avoiding publication of internal disputes or personnel controversies (the memorandum followed resignations of overseas officials whom Davis felt had assumed too much authority). Anti-pattern: leaking internal rows or seeking press attention for agency personnel/actions rather than focusing on intended overseas information objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: British wartime censorship rule on advance notices
rubrics_metrics.description: "British censorship prohibits the transmission from England of specific advance notices of Churchill's appearances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear procedural restriction for journalists and wire services during wartime: do not publish or transmit specific advance notices of the Prime Minister's (or other sensitive officials') scheduled public appearances. Practical effect noted in copy: dispatches under this censorship only confirm that an appearance is scheduled without providing advance specifics. Use-case: withholds operational/advance details to protect security and public-order considerations; anti-pattern: publishing precise advance schedules or locations that censors would suppress.
